albums.blurb: Tycho is the one-man project of San Francisco producer Scott Hansen, who is equally known as the graphic designer ISO50 and whose sunset-hued album art is as much a signature as his sound. Dive, released on Ghostly International in November 2011, is his second studio album and the record that fixed the Tycho template: warm analog synthesizers and hardware sound generators layered with guitar and bass into unhurried, fully instrumental pieces, a sound reviewers often place next to Boards of Canada. He later toured it front to back for its tenth anniversary.
albums.reception: The album holds a Metacritic score of 80, denoting generally favorable reviews, and PopMatters rated it 8/10 and called it one of the best electronic releases of 2011.

albums.blurb: The self-produced Montreal trio of Emmanuelle Proulx, Jessy Caron and Dragos Chiriac released Equus Caballus independently in May 2025, two months after its quieter companion Equus Asinus; the two horse-named records form a deliberate pair and together mark the band's most prolific year. Caballus is the livelier half, folding the murmured vocals and liquid bass of their earlier records into brisker, occasionally post-punk-tinged songs like the single "Billy Toppy".
albums.reception: The Daily Californian's review rated it 4.0/5, writing that the album traces its themes of devotion and dread with grace.

albums.blurb: One of two albums Simone released for Philips in 1965 alongside the big-band-leaning I Put a Spell on You, Pastel Blues is the stripped-down, blues-rooted half of that year's work, cut with her touring band and reaching from "Trouble in Mind" to a harrowing "Strange Fruit". It closes with the ten-minute "Sinnerman", the traditional spiritual whose arrangement here became one of her defining recordings and, decades later, a fixture of film and television.
albums.reception: The album reached No. 8 on Billboard's R&B albums chart and No. 139 on the Billboard 200, and a retrospective Pitchfork review scored it 8.7/10.
